key_insight: A fixed multi-layer quantum extreme learning machine can generate target distributions by training only a linear readout, but matches rather than outperforms a same-size classical random Fourier feature model.
engineering_relevance: Keeping the quantum reservoir fixed eliminates quantum-circuit optimization and gradients through the device, simplifying training while retaining measurement costs.
method: Map a scalar latent variable to measured expectation values using a fixed, randomly initialized quantum reservoir.
Train a linear readout by minimizing maximum mean discrepancy between generated and target samples.
Encode class labels on dedicated qubits for conditional generation with a shared readout.
evidence_signal: The study demonstrates one- and two-dimensional distribution generation and handwritten-digit generation from Digits and MNIST using a six-qubit reservoir; physical Hamiltonian dynamics preserve performance when inputs spread across the register.
watch_item: No quantum advantage is demonstrated at the studied sizes, and performance depends on reservoir dynamics spreading the encoded input.
paper_title: Generative Models using Multi-layer Quantum Extreme Learning Machines
